title: DIO/ODI Research Genealogy Registry
description: A source-linked, author-curated reconstruction of the research object, exploratory process, milestones, and intermediate artefacts through which Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and the Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI) emerged.
scope: Research-object, research-process, concept-emergence, and exploratory-artefact provenance. The registry complements the author-maintained professional ethnography and the publication corpus metadata.

research_objects.title: Od pultu přes ZUR a PSY až k SEO a copy s ostrými hroty! AI a dál…
research_objects.description: An evolving, layered representation of professional experience, knowledge, practice, and digital traces. Its research object is distributed across narrative text, explicit interpretive guidance, visual and semantic structures, linked sources, machine-readable metadata, and a dated changelog.
components: narrative text and non-linear professional trajectory
visual semantic map of page elements
AI-use notice and machine-readable agent instructions
structured page metadata and semantic markup
research_objects.role_in_genealogy: Primary research object examined through iterative AI-assisted secondary exploration.

research_objects.title: Marketing pro AI startupy & SaaS: copywriting a SEO pro vývojáře LLM a aplikací umělé inteligence
research_objects.description: An author-written professional article about marketing, copywriting, and SEO for AI startups and SaaS products. Its section 'Vztah k jednotlivým AI: zhola subjektivně a děsně útržkovitě' compares major AI systems through practical use, strengths, limitations, and workarounds.
components: comparative discussion of ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, Mistral AI, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Gemini, and Monica.im
practical observations on Czech-language processing, text generation, research, and daily professional use
source material for an eight-slide SlideShare presentation
research_objects.role_in_genealogy: A later professional article and source object for a SlideShare presentation. It documents the author's comparative AI practice and forms part of the wider exploratory archive, but postdates the May–June 2026 articulation of DIO and ODI.

research_processes.title: AI-assisted secondary exploration of the professional-ethnography object

temporal_scope.basis: Author-maintained changelog milestones; individual exploratory artefacts may have separate or undetermined dates.

research_processes.summary: The professional ethnography became the subject of iterative secondary exploration through AI-assisted machine readings and model-generated interpretations. These readings were examined in relation to the source text and its context. Their cross-domain associations, interpretive discrepancies, implicit readings, and algorithmic noise became material for the author's inquiry. The exploratory process contributed to the discovery and articulation of DIO, followed by the differentiation and articulation of ODI as its broader theoretical layer.
process_characteristics: iterative rather than strictly linear inquiry
secondary exploration of an existing multimodal source object
comparison of interpretations with the source text and surrounding context
attention to implicit meaning, cross-domain associations, and interpretive discrepancies
authorial synthesis and progressive conceptual articulation

roles.author: Research direction, selection and contextualization of source material, interpretation of model outputs, and conceptual synthesis.
roles.ai_systems: Generative and analytical systems used to produce secondary readings and expose patterns, associations, and interpretive differences in the source object.

subsequent_research.title: DIO to DIO — model-specific reconstruction analyses

milestones.title: The professional-ethnography text begins
milestones.summary: Initial work on the text and first outlines establish the evolving professional-ethnography object.

milestones.title: Interpretive methodology and visual semantic map are added
milestones.summary: The page gains an explicit interpretive note and a semantic map of visual elements, making parts of its layered reading context more explicit.

milestones.title: Executive Summary and semantic inventory are added
milestones.summary: The source object gains an Executive Summary and a semantic inventory, adding further explicit orientation and structured context for its interpretation.

milestones.title: AI-use context and machine-readable agent instructions are added
milestones.summary: The page's AI-use notice is refined and a machine-readable instruction layer for AI agents is added.

milestones.title: Digital Identity Optimization is articulated
milestones.summary: The professional-ethnography text is described as having organically connected a broad interdisciplinary field into a new disciplinary concept. DIO receives its own place in the text structure, and work on its Manifest begins. The changelog explicitly describes the professional ethnography as the empirical and asynchronous foundation from which DIO was derived.

milestones.title: Language differences, interdisciplinarity, and implicitness are added to the methodological reflection
milestones.summary: The methodology note is extended to address differences between Czech and English, interdisciplinarity, and implicitness in the source text.

milestones.title: Ontology of Digital Identity is articulated as the broader theoretical layer
milestones.summary: During work on DIO, a more general theoretical layer is distinguished from the applied focus of optimization and articulated as Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI).

artefacts.title: AIs: zhola subjektivně a děsně útržkovitě
artefacts.uploader_attribution: SEO specialista a copywriter Daniel Beránek
artefacts.research_role: An eight-slide presentation adapted from the author's article on marketing for AI startups and SaaS. It condenses the article's subjective comparison of major LLM and AI systems, including Czech-language handling, text generation, practical strengths, limitations, and workarounds. It is a later professional AI-practice artefact, not a direct milestone in the May–June 2026 emergence of DIO/ODI.
artefacts.summary: The SlideShare page explicitly identifies the presentation as being based on the author's source article. It covers ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, Mistral AI, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Gemini, and Monica.im.
